prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1078; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. Driver is confirmed as a named driver on the policy.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was inside the vehicle at the time of impact and that the collision happened as described. Photographs taken at the scene were reviewed and show the other driver's account matches the position of both cars.

Entry 3: Damage to the rear bumper and tailgate is consistent with the impact described and with the force reported by the other driver. No prior damage to this area of the vehicle appears in the file, and nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck and upper back pain consistent with whiplash from the impact. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the medical history provided, and the injury pattern fits the kind and force of the crash.

Entry 5: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, with physiotherapy and follow-up visits continuing. Counsel has been asked for the treatment records and an update on expected recovery. Claimant has added some small details since the first statement, but the core account has not changed.

Entry 6: File reviewed against the policy and the loss facts; all coverage conditions appear to be met. Reserve set pending receipt of medical records and the attorney's demand package. Next review scheduled once those documents arrive.
